### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **3** package(s): `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **49** documentable anchor(s).

**33** hand-written doc(s) name something this change touched — list omitted above 15 rows. Re-derive on the tree named below: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01598d936f47378c02354a9c20cb08f0346a8c2c`.

⛔ **11** release-owned page(s) also affected — read-only, see AGENTS.md Documentation Guardrails.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** cross-cutting symbol(s) contributed no route anchor: `resolveExecCtx (35 routes)`
- the SDK route bridge reached **65** of **247** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **44** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01598d936f47378c02354a9c20cb08f0346a8c2c` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `c224ea26019eb65d1fe342b41df07057c70e594a` — the merge of head `0f5f95d08060d9c68390c6fe4f11bfece0ffb084` into base `01598d936f47378c02354a9c20cb08f0346a8c2c`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin c224ea26019eb65d1fe342b41df07057c70e594a && git checkout c224ea26019eb65d1fe342b41df07057c70e594a
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 01598d936f47378c02354a9c20cb08f0346a8c2c 0f5f95d08060d9c68390c6fe4f11bfece0ffb084 && git checkout -B drift-repro 01598d936f47378c02354a9c20cb08f0346a8c2c && git merge --no-ff 0f5f95d08060d9c68390c6fe4f11bfece0ffb084

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 01598d936f47378c02354a9c20cb08f0346a8c2c
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 01598d936f47378c02354a9c20cb08f0346a8c2c` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

- Bare and execution read of a package-less row whose key only disabled packages hold: 200 to the withheld item (404). Right: `packagelessRowWithheldHolder` asks the registry's owner rule over every holder, and `null` (no holder at the key) stays served.

- File surface: 8 files. `protocol.ts`, `protocol-save.ts` and `registry-question.ts` are untouched; `registry.ts` is read only.
- The rejection pins assert status and code together on both transports, and that no body names the disabled package. The ablation counts match the pins as written: 7 for the #33401 arm, 18 x 2 + 14 = 50 for the mark, 4 for the door's withheld check.
- Check-runs when read: 22 success, 16 skipped, 0 failed, 11 in progress (Test Core 1/8 to 8/8, Build Core, Type Check workspace, Type Check consumer gates). This record holds no verdict for those 11.

### ② Semver level

- `patch` on metadata-protocol, rest and runtime with `Metadata-protocol: none`: right. objectql is test-only.
- Kit: `!` in the title and the changeset summary, present. **BREAKING** banner in both, present. ADR-0087 marker, exactly one. Dogfood battery full and green, pinned to `00d7daf5`; this head differs from it by one changeset line (N1). `Skills-docs:` line absent (S3).
- `Clause-②: no (narrowing)` holds only if S1 closes in code. If the draft cell stays, the diff also widens, and that line and "No answer widens" are wrong.

### ③ Boundary flags

- Clause-② moved from the claim's `no`: accepted in kind, subject to S1.
- The objectql test file extension: the approval is the dev's word, on neither card. Accepted; #32849 edits it and the face file too, so the later lander merges.
- Ten commits, one merge of `main`, one extra bare read on the disabled-only path: accepted.
- Full suites last ran at 6665c856: the in-progress Test Core shards answer that.
- Ablations predate the `findOne` revert: accepted; the CONTROL asserts the bare read serves the row first.
- Out-of-scope action-envelope finding (same on `main`): escalated to the seat. #33401's acceptance names that CONTROL, so a card must exist before `Fixes #33401` closes it (N2).
- 14 of 18 types answer 404 in the stored-row fixture: accepted as behaviour (N3).
- `open_questions`: none.

### ④ Design judgment

The narrowing makes a declared refusal real. ADR-0150 D3: a disabled package holds no name. D4 and R15: a package-less row over a package-held name is that holder's customization. Ruling 6882483833: withhold it, serve the environment's own item. Nothing declared is taken at the consumer; the row is kept and returns on re-enable. Probes, read in the tree:

- Environment's own item: admitted before the mark, and the face's arm answers `null`. Holds.
- Both holders disabled: binding `undefined`, then `disabledOnlyHolderOf`, withheld; `_env` marked, 404. Holds.
- One of two disabled: the 409 is unmarked and names only the enabled holder. Unchanged.
- Package-less caller: the bare read is that caller; both faces pinned. Holds.

S1 (should-fix) — the `_env` door judges with the active read, then admits a draft read. `admitEnvironmentAddress` (both doors) calls `getMetaItem` with type, name and member only; the admitted read keeps `?state=draft` and `?preview=draft`. Read, not run: X is the only registry holder and disabled, and enabled package Y holds only a draft row of the name. `strictDraftReadAddress` answers Y (`packagelessAddress` counts rows alone), the item is stamped Y, and no arm of the face withholds it. `main` answers 409; this head answers 200 with Y's draft at the environment's address, the case the door's own comment says stays refused. Undeclared, unpinned, a widening. Fix: carry state and preview into the judging read, or refuse a marked draft read; pin both transports.

S2 (should-fix) — a third `_env` door keeps the old answer. `packages/rest/src/import-mapping.ts#namedMappingRead` calls `admitEnvironmentQualifier` for `mappingName: "_env/NAME"`, and its docblock promises the answer of `GET /meta/mapping/_env/NAME`. It does not read the mark: the import door still answers 409 naming the disabled package where `/meta` now answers 404. Fix: admit there the same way, or file the card and name the open door in the changeset.

S3 (should-fix) — `Skills-docs:` is missing from the PR body and the changeset; a `(narrowing)` owes it (`content/docs/data-modeling/import-mappings.mdx` documents the `_env` 409).

N1 (nit) — the battery pin names `00d7daf5`, not this head; accepted deviation.
N2 (nit) — the action CONTROL of #33401 is unpinned; follow-up card owed by the seat.
N3 (nit) — the stored-row 409 CONTROL is live on 4 types only.

No must-fix.

ADR-0150 D4 and R15 make a package-less row over a package-held name that holder's customization; ruling 6882483833 counts every holder, disabled included, and puts the member outside the key. The face's new arm reads the registry's one owner rule over every holder, which is that ruling. The `_env` design (refuse in the synchronous protocol method, mark, let the door ask the asynchronous read) is sound, and the door's second read is the same request the admitted read then makes.

S1 (should-fix) — the lists are a sibling door this diff neither moves, pins nor declares. Read, not run: the unscoped list's disabled-holder filter (`protocol-meta-list-reads.ts`, the `disabledHolderListing` call) keeps every item bound to no package, and a stored package-less row at a member no enabled package ships seats a slot of its own in the merge. So with the only holder disabled, `GET /meta/:type` and the execution list would still carry the row whose by-name read now answers 404. Before this diff both served it; after it they disagree, against the list's own stated rule that the list and the by-name read hide the same items, and against the PR body's sentence that a disabled package's customization is never served. The sibling fix for the pair's row (#32354) pinned list and send beside the by-name read; this one pins neither. Fix: measure it on the #33401 fixture; then move the lists, or file the card and name the open door in the changeset and PR body.

S2 (should-fix) — the PR body and the verification kit describe an earlier head. The body has no `Skills-docs:` line (owed on a `(narrowing)`), no row for the import door, and states the `_env` cell without the three reads that keep 409. Its builds, 73 gates, ablations and dogfood battery are pinned to `00d7daf5`; four later commits change door code in rest and runtime, and none of the new arms (the draft-switch judgment, the import door's admission) carries an ablation. The seat's checklist asks for the battery at the head. All of this closes without moving the head, except new ablation evidence if the lane chooses to add pins.

S3 (should-fix) — the write side is not declared. The changeset says what happens to an existing row. It does not say what a save or delete at such a name does while every holder is disabled. Read, not run: the save door has no disabled-holder judgment for these types, so a package-less save is accepted and its read-back answers 404. That already held on `main` at a member the holder ships; this diff extends it to members it does not. Fix: one changeset sentence saying a save is kept and hidden until re-enable (or measure and correct me), and a pin.

S4 (should-fix) — the residual `_env` 409 names the disabled package. With an admitted draft switch or `?layers=`, and whenever the judging read serves or refuses, the answer is the marked refusal, whose only candidate is the disabled holder; the enabled package that actually holds the name through its stored row is not named.
